title: Session fragmentation resilience retro and delivery-guarantee action plan
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Post-incident follow-up for a multi-region streaming outage that produced client-visible partial token streams and session fragmentation during a capacity surge. This ticket consolidates the retro findings, documents temporary mitigations applied during the incident, and tracks the prioritized engineering work to prevent recurrence and improve end-to-end delivery guarantees.
impact_summary: During a cross-region capacity event, a subset of long-lived streaming sessions experienced truncated outputs (partial tokens) and client reconnections that produced duplicated or missing token fragments. Impacted customers reported degraded chat continuity and higher error rates for streaming endpoints. Estimated user-facing error rate peaked at ~0.8% for active streaming sessions during the incident window.
timeline_summary: 2026-02-28 10:12 UTC: first increase in streaming p99 latency observed. 2026-02-28 10:20 UTC: head-of-line queueing on GPU worker queues detected; first partial-token reports from customers. 2026-02-28 10:34 UTC: automated circuit breaker escalated some requests to fallback models, but in-flight sessions were not reconciled, leading to session fragments. 2026-02-28 11:05 UTC: mitigations (short-lived async drain, temporary rate-limits per-tenant) rolled out. 2026-02-28 11:40 UTC: incident declared resolved after traffic shaping and worker scaling completed.
root_cause: A congestion event exposed a race between the streaming write path and the session commit path: when a worker hit quota ceilings and the request router executed a fallback policy, the in-memory session state was partially flushed to a short-lived cache and the client-side reconnection flow replayed without a reliable token-commit handshake. Backpressure signals were not propagated across the router->worker->session manager boundary, causing head-of-line blocking and token fragmentation across reconnections.
mitigations_completed: Applied per-tenant emergency rate-limits to reduce head-of-line blocking
Enabled a short delay drain on router to prefer graceful worker handoffs
Deployed a hotfix to mark partial-session fragments as resumable rather than final
Updated incident runbook with immediate steps to enable fallback-safe session draining
open_action_items: Implement idempotent token-commit protocol between worker and session manager (owner: Marcus Lee, estimate: 5)
Propagate explicit backpressure signals across the routing layer and worker pool (owner: Clara Rodriguez, estimate: 3)
Add an at-most-once reconnection handshake for clients to detect and request missing token ranges (owner: Evan Kim, estimate: 5)
Introduce per-session priority lanes to avoid single-tenant head-of-line blocking (owner: Priya Shah, estimate: 8)
Create synthetic canary that injects transient capacity loss and validates session continuity end-to-end (owner: Marcus Lee, estimate: 3)
Expand streaming SLOs and alert thresholds to include partial-token rates and resumed-session mismatch rates (owner: Observability team, estimate: 2)
Run a game-day (load test) simulating regional degradation before runtime-1.21 rollout (owner: Reliability eng, due: 2026-03-25)
Update SDK guidance and add client reconnection examples documenting resumable-session semantics (owner: Developer Experience, estimate: 2)
Schedule security review for idempotent commit changes that touch session encryption and KMS interactions (owner: Security, due: 2026-03-20)
Postmortem writeup and customer-facing incident summary to be published after action items reach >=50% completion (owner: Aisha Patel, estimate: 1)
test_plan: Unit tests for token-commit idempotency and conflict resolution
Integration test that replays client reconnects with controlled token gaps
Chaos test: kill a worker mid-stream and verify reconnection preserves token order and no duplication
Load test: multi-tenant traffic with enforced per-tenant bursts to validate priority lanes
monitoring_changes: Add tracing span to record 'session_commit' and 'session_resume' latency and status
Dashboard: session-continuity heatmap by region and model-version
rollout_plan: Feature branch -> canary on 'dedicated' region with 1% traffic
Observe for 48h with synthetic canary + production telemetry
Gradual ramp to 25% then 100% with automated rollback on continuity regressions
Maintain emergency toggle to disable new commit protocol and fall back to current behavior
notes: We chose idempotent commit over synchronous durable writes to avoid increasing tail latency; trade-off is more complex conflict resolution for rare races. Client SDK changes will be backwards compatible: servers will advertise resumable-session capability. Security review required because token metadata touches KMS-wrapped blobs.
status_updates: 2026-03-03: Scoping complete for idempotent commit protocol; proto design reviewed by Runtime and Session teams
2026-03-06: Emergency rate-limit thresholds converted to per-tenant dynamic values; monitoring added
2026-03-10: Hotfix to tag partial fragments as resumable deployed to prod and reduced customer reports by ~70%
2026-03-14: Action item owners assigned and schedule for game-day set; moving ticket to 'In Progress'
